correctness.rationale: The total number of partial matchings is N=n^3+2n+1 by choosing occupied rows and injecting them into columns. A specified edge occurs in Q=n^2-n+1 matchings because its endpoints leave K_{2,n-1}. The number of matchings with odd intersection with S is at most |S|Q, proving W>=N-2|S|Q. This is at least 2n for |S|<=r=(n+1)/2 when n is odd. If n is even, every multiplier has the parity of the odd N and cannot vanish. An r-edge row star attains the union bound since a matching uses at most one edge in that row. Appending an edge in another row but a selected column flips exactly those matching contributions containing the new edge. In the residual board K_{2,n-1}, omitting the star row has n completions, and using it has signed column sum (n-1)-2(r-1)=0 with the same number of remaining completions per chosen column. Thus the new support has W=2n-2n=0. When n>=3, r>=2 distinguishes the heavy row, so the 3 choices of heavy row, binomial(n,r) column selections, 2 extra rows and r extra-edge columns give distinct supports. This proves a lower bound on multiplicity, not a classification. Counting convolution has these unnormalized multipliers on the full Boolean edge group, so invertibility and injectivity statements follow. Both frozen verifiers and reported results were inspected, not executed. A separate direct signed-count run (python3 /workspace/review_checks.py 3) exhausts frequencies at n=3,4,5 (36 first zeros, none, and 270 first zeros, respectively), and checks selected boundary stars and their extensions through n=25. The proof, not these finite tests, covers all widths.
